messages:
maria: Heads up - prod inference p95 spiked from ~120ms to ~700ms for about 15m in us-west-2. Affected model: redwood-open-13b-quant on dedicated-pool-3. Traces are sparse; dashboard shows CPU utilization bump but the kernel-selection panels show gaps. Can someone take triage?

jonathan: on it. any correlation with deploys or config pushes ~2h ago?

maria: no deploys logged at that time from the deploy bot, but infra config push at ~2:05 that touched batching heuristics. thread_ts=1765012345

engbot: Alert recorded: inference-latency-spike (severity=high) - incident created #INC-2026

sara: I pulled a flame profile from one of the tails. many requests fell back to matmul_generic instead of matmul_fast. snippet from /var/log/runtime/kernel_select.log:
```
[2026-03-18T02:09:10Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-open-13b-quant seq_len=128 kernel_selected=matmul_generic reason=heuristic_mismatch
[2026-03-18T02:09:10Z] request_id=def456 model=redwood-open-13b-quant seq_len=32 kernel_selected=matmul_generic reason=heuristic_mismatch
```
That aligns with higher CPU and slower token throughput.

alex: why would heuristic flip during that window? the batching heuristic config changed max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 earlier. maybe it caused more frequent small batches and the selector chose a conservative path.

kevin: batcher metrics show a shift: median batch_size down from 12->4 around the same time. query I ran:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
Result: p95 batch size dropped to 6. That increases per-token overhead and forces non-optimized kernels for small matmuls.

maria: also saw KV cache activity increase. sample logs:
```
[2026-03-18T02:09:11Z] shard=3 kv_cache_evicted=true evict_reason=noisy_neighbor_load keys_evicted=214
```
If cache hit rate drops, we're recomputing KV and touching slower paths.

sara: big issue: distributed tracing sampling for prod was set to 10% last quarter to cut costs, and kernel-selection spans were excluded from sampled payloads by filter rule 'exclude_internal_selector'. that means our root cause signals were missing in the traces we retained.

jonathan: can we temporarily bump sampling for the affected service and region to 100% for 30m to capture another tail window?

maria: doing it now - increasing sampling to 100% for service=runtime, region=us-west-2. also enabling kernel-selection spans. will re-ingest to temporary index 'perf-debug'.

alex: as mitigation we can force runtime to prefer matmul_fast for seq_len>=32 until we fix the heuristic. runbook command:
```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  https://controlplane.internal/runtime/config \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-13b-quant","kernel_override":"matmul_fast","ttl":900}'
```

kevin: applied the override at 02:14 UTC. after override p95 dropped to ~160ms within two minutes and throughput normalized. monitoring graph: p95 -> 700ms -> 160ms.

maria: confirmed. temporary win. Next steps: revert the max_batch_tokens change, investigate batching heuristic logic (why it produced too many small batches), and add a guard that prevents kernel selector exclusion under low-sample conditions.

sara: action items I'm taking: 1) add unit tests for batching edge cases (token distribution spikes), 2) update tracing config: default sampling 20% with critical-path spans always-on, 3) add KV-eviction alert threshold (evicts/min > 50 -> P1). I'll open follow-up tickets.

jonathan: I'll roll back the batching config change and run a canary for 10min to validate. also adding an instrumentation metric 'kernel_fallback_count' to the runtime.

maria: can someone create a short postmortem after we stabilize? include timeline, what we changed, and the dashboard updates we want.

kevin: will file INC-2026 follow-up with runbook updates and attach profiling artifacts. pinging @infra-oncall for any infra-level remediation.

infra-oncall: saw the noisy neighbor on shard 3, we isolated the tenant and will throttle the noisy VM. added migration ticket to re-balance.

maria: thanks team - good catch. leave this thread open until dashboards show stable p95 < 200ms for 1h. :thumbsup: 

sara: retained traces in perf-debug index show kernel_reason=heuristic_mismatch spikes aligned with config change. will attach pointers in the follow-up ticket.
